# Document, PR and issue scenarios

Stage each scenario's test-files/ as its own workspace root, outside the plugin and
any SKILL.md ancestor. Load only the skill under test, its shared instructions and
the scenario prompt into a fresh editor session. Never stage eval.json or oracle/
with the editor: they contain grading expectations. For non-triggers, make the
skill description available for selection without preloading its body.

Cases 1–6 separate comprehension (the five neutral questions in oracle/expected.json)
from fidelity, source inspection and predeclared orientation/correctness defects.
Give fresh original and revised readers only the files in reader_manifest, with the
same questions and model/settings. A separate grader gets their answers, both
artifacts, requirements/source, the editor tool trace and oracle. Every assertion
needs PASS/FAIL/PARTIAL with evidence. Cases 7–10 grade routing and unchanged files;
reader comparison is not applicable.

Record staged hashes, exact allowed-file manifests, model/settings, raw tool traces,
answers and verdicts with the consuming project's verification evidence. Shared
filesystem access is not isolation: inspect traces for reads outside the manifest,
and invalidate leaked or incompletely traced runs. These are manual scenarios, not
an executable harness. Authored scenarios are not evidence of executed behavior.

## PR fixture setup

Cases 11–15 add PR increments, destination visibility and local output boundaries.
Cases 11–13 include `snapshots/base/` and `snapshots/head/`: before the editor runs,
create a separate staged Git repository at `checkout/`, commit the base snapshot
and name that revision `review-base`, then commit the head snapshot and name it
`review-head`. Leave head checked out. Preserve snapshot paths relative to each
snapshot root. Record the actual revision IDs and diff in the run evidence. These
are real local revisions; misleading stack labels in `context.md` are intentional.
The snapshots are staging inputs, not additional editor reading paths.

Give the editor staged non-snapshot files plus read-only access to `checkout/`,
including Git metadata for revision/diff queries. Never permit Git writes during
editing. URLs ending in `.invalid` and the PR bodies/access declarations are
synthetic read-only platform responses: do not contact a real service. Cases 12
and 15 use `remote-body.md` as immutable input; case 14 uses an immutable pasted
body capture. Case 12 includes an unrelated draft to test collision handling.

Cases 11–13 and 15 use original/revised readers. Resolve
`<produced-local-draft>` to the editor's actual output; `original_reader_manifest`
overrides `reader_manifest` for the original where present. Provide only the named
artifact: all five answers must be available there. Case 13's baseline answers
already pass; its declared disclosure defect still requires repair. Inspect the
editor's final report as well as its draft for private-fact leakage. Case 14 grades
clarification and unchanged files without a reader comparison. The separate grader
also receives the source snapshots, access declarations and actual Git evidence.

Case 13 requests a caller-only completion link to the selected local output by
absolute path. Grade that link separately from prohibited private source pointers;
the exception applies only to this completion message, never to the destination
draft or disclosure of restricted facts.

## Issue fixture setup

Cases 16–24 use supplied offline issue context, not PR base/head pairs. Stage only
each scenario's `test-files/` as an independent workspace. Do not initialize a PR
checkout, contact a tracker or expose the oracle to the editor. Editing cases
16–22 must not execute reproduction commands; execution cases 23/24 permit local

10: implementation and tests behind its claims. Repetition does not verify a claim.
11: Inspect supplied sources to explain the behavior,
12: conditions and rationale at the applicable revision. Follow relevant references
13: far enough to understand the claim, without recursively auditing the whole feature.
14: Reading a source does not authorize editing it or executing its commands.

18: names, stack annotations and task numbers do not establish the increment. Separate

25: versus established causes, and differences between reported and inspected versions.
26: Do not claim reproduction or passing tests without evidence. A supporting PR does
27: not turn issue editing into PR editing; no PR diff or future implementation is
28: required for an issue proposal.
29:

31: provide evidence of exercised cases, not proof of intent or complete coverage.
32: Distinguish accepted requirements, proposals, implemented behavior and future work.

34: invent runtime evidence. Reuse source understanding from the invoking session only
35: after checking that its scope and revision still apply; inspect missing or changed
36: context instead of repeating unrelated investigation.
37:

39: ask a focused question or retain a limitation in the artifact. Record the issue,
40: next step and known owner there or in an already-selected task document; identify
41: unknown owners.
42: Do not manufacture an answer, silently settle a product decision or create an extra
43: report to hide the gap. Continue independent, supported edits when possible.
44: If an issue body is unavailable, explain the access limit and request text or an
45: accessible source; write no purported revision. With a body but unavailable
46: supporting evidence, continue supported edits at an established destination,
47: preserving reported/proposed status and verification limits. An unresolved
48: destination requires a question before writing.
49: 
50: ## Establish protected meaning
51: 
52: Keep a working inventory of essential claims and their evidence; no separate ledger
53: is required. Preserve:
54: 
55: - Requirements, observable behavior, rationale, constraints and uncertainty.
56: - Mandatory versus optional language; conditions, exceptions and thresholds.
57: - Identifiers, interface shapes, ownership and decision provenance.
58: - Deployment gates, completion status, verification limits and unresolved decisions.
59: - Required document sections, domain-rubric topics, task checkboxes and dependencies.
60:

62: between accepted requirements and implementation must stay explicit: describe both
63: and the next action needed to reconcile them. Neither source automatically overrides
64: the other. Do not erase a requirement to make the prose agree with the code.
65:

67: 
68: 1. Explicit user/repository audience restrictions override tracking or reachability.
69: 2. For PR editing only, files tracked at the target repository's PR head are
70:    accessible to its established review audience, not automatically a wider one.
71:    For a GitHub issue identified with repository R, default to R's issue audience

96: answer, where relevant to the artifact:
97: 
98: 1. Why does this work exist?

102: 5. What still needs a decision?

107: after orientation. Remove duplication while retaining the detail needed for the
108: reader's task. Preserve the project's organization and document-type requirements;

110: questions. An explicit unknown can be the correct answer.

119: Bug reports retain supplied reproduction steps, commands, environment/version,
120: expected/observed results and frequency or conditions. Feature requests explain
121: the need, proposed or accepted outcome, scope, existing acceptance criteria and
122: open decisions; other types follow their purpose and organization. Do not impose
123: empty headings. Clarify existing criteria without inventing thresholds, scope
124: commitments, solution decisions or new criteria; missing decisions/criteria remain
125: unknown with the next step and known or explicitly unknown owner where relevant.
126:

128: in-scope links, including cross-file references. Check accessible inbound references
129: when changing headings; keep the anchor when callers outside scope would break, or
130: surface the wider change needed. Keep executable examples intact unless an
131: authorized, evidence-backed correction is verified. Do not change implementation,
132: run deployments or migrations, or make production or external writes.
133:

135: and structural requirements, leave it unchanged. Clear prose may still need a
136: factual or disclosure repair; passing the five reader questions alone is not a
137: reason to retain such a defect. Make only justified changes, without a word-count
138: reduction target or a new summary artifact.

141:

143: Check comprehension first: can the intended reader answer the applicable questions
144: through the artifact's intended reading path, without relying on the editor's hidden
145: context? Check the specific confusion motivating the edit, not just sentence length.
146:

148: qualification may disappear and no unsupported claim may appear. Recheck headings,
149: anchors, links, task state, required topics and executable examples affected by the
150: edit. For issues, also check reproduction details, qualifications, existing criteria
151: and decision status. Correct editorial regressions; keep unresolved source disagreements visible
152: with their next step. Fluent prose cannot compensate for lost meaning.
153: Recheck destination visibility, including facts paraphrased from restricted sources.
154: 
155: Report changed paths, whether the result was unchanged, and material evidence gaps
156: or wider edits needed. This is an in-session comparison, not independent fidelity
157: verification or proof of improved human comprehension. The caller owns further
158: review required by the project.

1: # Preparation settings
2: 
3: Set one default preparation time for your restaurant and give individual menu
4: items their own times when needed. This update determines which preparation time
5: applies to each item and saves that time when an order is created.
6: 
7: An item with no preparation time set uses the restaurant default. This is called
8: **inheritance**: the item uses the current default each time its preparation time
9: is looked up. Both a missing value and `null` mean no time is set. An item set to
10: **0 minutes** has its own preparation time of zero and does not inherit the default.
11: 
12: Each new order keeps a copy of the preparation time that applied when it was
13: created. Changing the restaurant default affects the next lookup for items that
14: inherit it; existing orders keep their saved time.
15:

17: time set uses 15 minutes, while an item explicitly set to zero uses 0 minutes.
18: An order created for the first item saves 15 minutes. If you then change the
19: default to **20 minutes**, that item's next lookup returns 20 minutes, and a new
20: order for it saves 20 minutes. The earlier order still has 15 minutes, and the
21: item set to zero still uses 0 minutes.
22: 
23: Scheduling is outside this update. The product owner still needs to decide
24: whether the menu editor should show inheritance badges to identify items that
25: use the restaurant default.
26: 
27: For technical reference, the preparation-time field is named `prep_minutes` on
28: restaurants, items and orders. `effective_minutes` determines the applicable time;
29: `create_order` copies it into a new order.
